module nupp.io.path.pathtext

--[[
Path text, as rules about characters.

Most operations `nupp.io.path` offers are questions about the text of a
path, and none of those needs the filesystem or the platform it is running on.
They were C, and being C meant each of them crossed the FFI, allocated an
answer, copied it back out and freed it -- for a path of a few dozen bytes,
which is what a path is. They now all live here; only the operating-system
queries for a working directory and a real path cross the filesystem boundary.

A path is read as a sequence of components: an optional prefix, an optional
root, and the names between separators, with `.` dropped and `..` kept. The
scans retain byte offsets rather than component records: several results are
slices of what the caller wrote rather than a rebuild. The parent of
`alpha/./beta/../file` is `alpha/./beta/..`, written that way, and normalizing
is a separate request with its own answer.

POSIX has one separator and no prefix. Windows has two separators and three
prefixes that matter: a drive, a UNC share, and the verbatim form, which is
carried and rebuilt but not otherwise reasoned about, since its whole point is
that the system does not normalize it either.

`windows` is a parameter here rather than the `#if` it was in C. These rules do
not depend on where they run, only on which set is asked for, and making that an
argument is what lets a machine of either kind test both.

Normalization has one ordinary Nupp body. An AOT build lowers its fresh table,
rooted string reads and string construction through the VM-aware construction
IR; an AOT-off or portable build runs those same authored operations as Lua.
]]

local pathtext = {}

--- What a component is. `.` never becomes one; `..` always does.
--- @export
const pathtext.PREFIX = 0

--- @export
const pathtext.ROOT = 1

--- @export
const pathtext.PARENT = 2

--- @export
const pathtext.NORMAL = 3

const byte = string.byte
const SLASH: integer = 47
const BACKSLASH: integer = 92
const DOT: integer = 46
const COLON: integer = 58

local function isSeparator(value: integer?, windows: boolean): boolean
    if value == nil then
        return false
    end

    return value == SLASH or (windows and value == BACKSLASH)
end

local function isDriveLetter(value: integer?): boolean
    if value == nil then
        return false
    end

    return (value >= 65 and value <= 90) or (value >= 97 and value <= 122)
end

--- Whether the path uses the verbatim form. The test is byte-exact:
--- the system recognizes `\\?\` and nothing else -- not `//?/`, and not `/` as
--- a separator after it -- so changing this text changes the path it names.
local function isVerbatim(text: string, windows: boolean): boolean
    if not windows or #text < 4 then
        return false
    end

    return byte(text, 1) == BACKSLASH
        and byte(text, 2) == BACKSLASH
        and byte(text, 3) == 63
        and byte(text, 4) == BACKSLASH
end

--- How many leading bytes of `text` are its prefix: none on POSIX, and on
--- Windows the drive, the share, or a verbatim or device marker together with
--- the disk, device or UNC share it names.
---
--- @param text the path
--- @param windows whether Windows rules apply
--- @return the prefix length, in bytes
function pathtext.prefixLength(text: string, windows: boolean): integer
    if not windows then
        return 0
    end
    local length = #text
    if length >= 2 and byte(text, 2) == COLON and isDriveLetter(byte(text, 1)) then
        return 2
    end
    if length >= 2 and isSeparator(byte(text, 1), windows) and isSeparator(byte(text, 2), windows) then
        local third = byte(text, 3)
        if length >= 4 and (third == 63 or third == DOT) and isSeparator(byte(text, 4), windows) then
            -- `\\?\` and `\\.\` carry the next component with them, as Windows
            -- and Rust's `Prefix` read them: the disk in `\\?\C:`, the device in
            -- `\\.\COM1`, and in `\\?\UNC\server\share` the server and share too.
            -- Stopping at the marker made `C:` a name, so the parent of
            -- `\\?\C:\foo` was `\\?\C:`, which names the raw volume rather than
            -- its root directory.
            local at: integer = 4
            local parts: integer = 1
            local seen: integer = 0
            while seen < parts do
                local begin = at + 1
                while at < length and not isSeparator(byte(text, at + 1), windows) do
                    at = at + 1
                end
                seen = seen + 1
                if seen == 1 and third == 63 and at - begin == 2 and text:sub(begin, at):upper() == "UNC" then
                    parts = 3
                end
                if seen < parts then
                    if at == length then
                        break
                    end
                    at = at + 1
                end
            end

            return at
        end

        -- A share reaches past the server and the share name both.
        local at: integer = 2
        local seen: integer = 0
        while seen < 2 do
            while at < length and not isSeparator(byte(text, at + 1), windows) do
                at = at + 1
            end
            seen = seen + 1
            if seen < 2 then
                while at < length and isSeparator(byte(text, at + 1), windows) do
                    at = at + 1
                end
                if at == length then
                    break
                end
            end
        end

        return at
    end

    return 0
end

--- Whether a path is anchored at a root. This is deliberately answered from
--- its leading bytes: constructing every component to inspect the first one is
--- the dominant cost for this otherwise constant-time question.
---
--- @param text the path
--- @param windows whether Windows rules apply
--- @return whether the path is absolute
function pathtext.isAbsolute(text: string, windows: boolean): boolean
    local prefix = pathtext.prefixLength(text, windows)
    local rooted = prefix < #text and isSeparator(byte(text, prefix + 1), windows)
    if windows and prefix >= 2 and byte(text, 2) == COLON then
        return rooted
    end

    return prefix ~= 0 or rooted
end

--- An answer on its way out.
---
--- Windows writes a separator either way and returns one, so what it wrote is
--- rewritten here. POSIX does not, and must not: a backslash there is an
--- ordinary byte in an ordinary name. A verbatim path is Windows's own
--- exception: the system reads `\\?\` and its backslashes literally, so the
--- answer keeps every byte as it was written.
---
--- @param value the text to answer with
--- @param windows whether Windows rules apply
--- @return the text, with separators in the answer's form
function pathtext.finish(value: string, windows: boolean): string
    if not windows or isVerbatim(value, windows) then
        return value
    end

    return (value:gsub("\\", "/"))
end

            at = at - 1
        end
        local start = at + 1
        local width = finish - start + 1
        if not (width == 1 and byte(text, start) == DOT) then
            local kind = width == 2 and byte(text, start) == DOT and byte(text, start + 1) == DOT and pathtext.PARENT
                or pathtext.NORMAL
            return start, width, kind, anchored
        end
    end

    if rooted then
        return prefix + 1, 1, pathtext.ROOT, anchored
    elseif prefix ~= 0 then
        return 1, prefix, pathtext.PREFIX, anchored
    end

    return nil, 0, nil, anchored
end

local function beforeLast(text: string, start: integer, anchored: integer, windows: boolean): integer
    local at = start - 1
    while at > anchored and isSeparator(byte(text, at), windows) do
        at = at - 1
    end

    return at
end

local function splitNameAt(text: string, start: integer, length: integer): (integer, integer?, integer)
    local at = length
    while at > 0 do
        at = at - 1
        if byte(text, start + at) == DOT then
            if at == 0 then
                return length, nil, 0
            end

            return at, start + at + 1, length - at - 1
        end
    end

    return length, nil, 0
end

--- Appends a part, replacing what came before when the part says so.
---
--- An absolute part names a place of its own, and on Windows a part with a
--- prefix does too, while a rooted part without one keeps the prefix and nothing
--- else. The part is appended as it was written rather than as it parsed:
--- pushing keeps a trailing separator or a `.` the caller put there, and
--- normalizing is a separate request.
---
--- @param carried what has been joined so far
--- @param part the part to append
--- @param windows whether Windows rules apply
--- @return the joined text
function pathtext.pushPart(carried: string, part: string, windows: boolean): string
    local prefix = pathtext.prefixLength(part, windows)
    local rooted = prefix ~= 0 or (#part ~= 0 and isSeparator(byte(part, 1), windows))
    local head = carried
    if rooted then
        head = ""
        if prefix == 0 then
            local currentPrefix = pathtext.prefixLength(carried, windows)
            if currentPrefix ~= 0 then
                head = carried:sub(1, currentPrefix)
            end
        end
    elseif #carried ~= 0 and not isSeparator(byte(carried, #carried), windows) then
        -- A bare drive prefix names a coordinate system rather than a place, so a
        -- part joined onto one stays drive-relative: `C:` and `foo` make `C:foo`,
        -- not the absolute `C:/foo`. A share prefix names a place, and a separator
        -- still belongs between it and what follows. A verbatim path gets the
        -- one separator the system reads there, since `/` is an ordinary byte
        -- after `\\?\`.
        local currentPrefix = pathtext.prefixLength(carried, windows)
        if currentPrefix ~= #carried or byte(carried, #carried) ~= COLON then
            head = carried .. (isVerbatim(carried, windows) and "\\" or "/")
        end
    end

    return head .. part
end

--- Joins parts under the platform's rules.
---
--- @param parts the parts to join, in order
--- @param windows whether Windows rules apply
--- @return the joined path
function pathtext.join(parts: {string}, windows: boolean): string
    local carried = ""
    for _, part in ipairs(parts) do
        carried = pathtext.pushPart(carried, part, windows)
    end

    return pathtext.finish(carried, windows)
end

-- Advances one allocation-free component cursor. Phase zero offers the prefix,
-- phase one the root, and phase two the ordinary components after dropping `.`
-- and repeated separators.
local function nextComponent(
    text: string,
    at: integer,
    phase: integer,
    windows: boolean
): (integer?, integer, integer?, integer, integer)
    local length = #text
    if phase == 0 then
        local prefix = pathtext.prefixLength(text, windows)
        at, phase = prefix, 1
        if prefix ~= 0 then
            return 1, prefix, pathtext.PREFIX, at, phase
        end
    end
    if phase == 1 then
        phase = 2
        if at < length and isSeparator(byte(text, at + 1), windows) then
            local start = at + 1
            while at < length and isSeparator(byte(text, at + 1), windows) do
                at = at + 1
            end

            return start, 1, pathtext.ROOT, at, phase
        end
    end
    while at < length do
        local start = at + 1
        while at < length and not isSeparator(byte(text, at + 1), windows) do
            at = at + 1
        end
        local width = at - start + 1
        if width ~= 0 and not (width == 1 and byte(text, start) == DOT) then
            local kind = width == 2 and byte(text, start) == DOT and byte(text, start + 1) == DOT and pathtext.PARENT
                or pathtext.NORMAL
            while at < length and isSeparator(byte(text, at + 1), windows) do
                at = at + 1
            end

            return start, width, kind, at, phase
        end
        while at < length and isSeparator(byte(text, at + 1), windows) do
            at = at + 1
        end
    end

    return nil, 0, nil, at, phase
end

local function appendComponent(
    answer: string,
    needsSeparator: boolean,
    text: string,
    start: integer,
    length: integer,
    kind: integer
): (string, boolean)
    if kind == pathtext.PREFIX then
        return answer .. text:sub(start, start + length - 1), false
    elseif kind == pathtext.ROOT then
        return answer .. "/", false
    end

    return answer .. (needsSeparator and "/" or "") .. text:sub(start, start + length - 1), true
end

--- Rebuilds a path's component view without resolving `..`.
---
--- This is the textual half of making a path absolute: duplicate separators
--- and `.` disappear, while `..` remains because resolving it across a symbolic
--- link requires the filesystem. A verbatim path is answered unchanged, for
--- the same reason `normalize` leaves one alone.
--- @param text the path
--- @param windows whether Windows rules apply
--- @return the cleaned path
function pathtext.clean(text: string, windows: boolean): string
    if isVerbatim(text, windows) then
        return text
    end
    local answer = ""
    local needsSeparator = false
    local at: integer = 0
    local phase: integer = 0
    while true do
        local start, length, kind, nextAt, nextPhase = nextComponent(text, at, phase, windows)
        if start == nil then
            break
        end
        answer, needsSeparator = appendComponent(
            answer,
            needsSeparator,
            text,
            start as integer,
            length,
            kind as integer
        )
        at, phase = nextAt, nextPhase
    end

    return pathtext.finish(answer, windows)
end

--- Expresses `target` against `base` using their component views.
---
--- A target that is its base returns `.`: the path is where the base already
--- is, and `.` represents that location, where `""` names nothing a filesystem
--- call accepts. A verbatim path is refused, because expressing one is exactly
--- the reasoning about its components this module does not do.
--- @param target the path to express
--- @param base the path to express it against
--- @param windows whether Windows rules apply
--- @return the relative path, or nil when the coordinate systems differ
--- @return a failure reason, when there is no relative form
function pathtext.relative(target: string, base: string, windows: boolean): (string?, string?)
    if isVerbatim(target, windows) or isVerbatim(base, windows) then
        return nil, "a verbatim path is carried rather than reasoned about"
    end
    local targetAbsolute = pathtext.isAbsolute(target, windows)
    local baseAbsolute = pathtext.isAbsolute(base, windows)
    if targetAbsolute ~= baseAbsolute then
        if targetAbsolute then
            return pathtext.clean(target, windows), nil
        end

        return nil, "paths do not share a relative coordinate system"
    end

    local targetAt: integer, targetPhase: integer = 0, 0
    local baseAt: integer, basePhase: integer = 0, 0
    local targetStart, targetLength, targetKind, nextTargetAt, nextTargetPhase = nextComponent(
        target,
        targetAt,
        targetPhase,
        windows
    )
    local baseStart, baseLength, baseKind, nextBaseAt, nextBasePhase = nextComponent(base, baseAt, basePhase, windows)
    while targetStart ~= nil and baseStart ~= nil do
        if targetKind ~= baseKind or targetLength ~= baseLength then
            break
        end
        -- A root is compared by kind alone: `/` and `\` name the same anchor. A
        -- prefix is compared with its separators folded the same way, so a share
        -- written with either separator still matches itself.
        if targetKind ~= pathtext.ROOT then
            local targetPart = target:sub(targetStart as integer, (targetStart as integer) + targetLength - 1)
            local basePart = base:sub(baseStart as integer, (baseStart as integer) + baseLength - 1)
            if targetKind == pathtext.PREFIX then
                targetPart = pathtext.finish(targetPart, windows)
                basePart = pathtext.finish(basePart, windows)
            end
            if targetPart ~= basePart then
                break
            end
        end
        targetAt, targetPhase = nextTargetAt, nextTargetPhase
        baseAt, basePhase = nextBaseAt, nextBasePhase
        targetStart, targetLength, targetKind, nextTargetAt, nextTargetPhase = nextComponent(
            target,
            targetAt,
            targetPhase,
            windows
        )
        baseStart, baseLength, baseKind, nextBaseAt, nextBasePhase = nextComponent(base, baseAt, basePhase, windows)
    end

    -- Diverging at a prefix or a root means the paths are anchored in different
    -- coordinate systems, and no count of `..` steps leads from one to the other.
    if baseStart ~= nil
        and (
            baseKind == pathtext.PREFIX
            or baseKind == pathtext.ROOT
            or (targetStart ~= nil and (targetKind == pathtext.PREFIX or targetKind == pathtext.ROOT))
        )
    then
        return nil, "paths do not share a relative coordinate system"
    end

    local parents: integer = 0
    while baseStart ~= nil do
        if baseKind == pathtext.PARENT then
            return nil, "paths do not share a relative coordinate system"
        end
        parents = parents + 1
        baseAt, basePhase = nextBaseAt, nextBasePhase
        baseStart, baseLength, baseKind, nextBaseAt, nextBasePhase = nextComponent(base, baseAt, basePhase, windows)
    end

    local answer = ""
    local needsSeparator = false
    for _ = 1, parents do
        answer = answer .. (needsSeparator and "/" or "") .. ".."
        needsSeparator = true
    end
    while targetStart ~= nil do
        answer, needsSeparator = appendComponent(
            answer,
            needsSeparator,
            target,
            targetStart as integer,
            targetLength,
            targetKind as integer
        )
        targetAt, targetPhase = nextTargetAt, nextTargetPhase
        targetStart, targetLength, targetKind, nextTargetAt, nextTargetPhase = nextComponent(
            target,
            targetAt,
            targetPhase,
            windows
        )
    end
    if #answer == 0 then
        -- No steps up and none along: the target is its base.
        answer = "."
    end

    return pathtext.finish(answer, windows), nil
end

--- Replaces the final name, or the extension on it.
---
--- The name is dropped where there is one and kept where there is not, which is
--- what makes `a/b` become `a/c` and `a/..` become `a/../c`. An extension put on
--- a path with no name to carry it leaves the path as its own answer.
---
--- @param text the path
--- @param replacement the new name, or the new extension
--- @param extension whether the replacement is an extension rather than a name
--- @param windows whether Windows rules apply
--- @return the derived path
--- @raises string when the replacement is not one component: a name that is
---     empty, `.` or `..`, or either one holding a separator or a NUL byte.
---     Under Windows rules a colon is refused too, because the system reads it
---     as a drive or a stream rather than as part of the name.
function pathtext.with(text: string, replacement: string, extension: boolean, windows: boolean): string
    local what = extension and "an extension" or "a file name"
    if not extension and (replacement == "" or replacement == "." or replacement == "..") then
        error("nupp: " .. what .. " must be one path component, not " .. ("%q"):format(replacement), 3)
    end
    for at = 1, #replacement do
        local value = byte(replacement, at)
        if value == 0 or isSeparator(value, windows) or (windows and value == COLON) then
            error("nupp: " .. what .. " must be one path component, not " .. ("%q"):format(replacement), 3)
        end
    end

    local start, length, kind, anchored = lastComponent(text, windows)
    local hasName = start ~= nil and kind == pathtext.NORMAL
    if extension then
        if not hasName then
            return pathtext.finish(text, windows)
        end
        -- Everything up to the end of the stem, in the caller's own text,
        -- and then the new extension on the end of it.
        local found = start as integer
        local stemLength = splitNameAt(text, found, length)
        local head = text:sub(1, found - 1 + stemLength)
        if #replacement == 0 then
            return pathtext.finish(head, windows)
        end

        return pathtext.finish(head .. "." .. replacement, windows)
    end
    local head = hasName and text:sub(1, beforeLast(text, start as integer, anchored, windows)) or text
    if #head ~= 0 and not isSeparator(byte(head, #head), windows) then
        head = head .. (isVerbatim(head, windows) and "\\" or "/")
    end

    return pathtext.finish(head .. replacement, windows)
end

--- A named piece of a path: its parent, its file name, the stem of that name,
--- or the extension on it.
---
--- Each is a slice of what the caller wrote rather than a rebuild, because
--- asking for a path's parent asks about that path and not about the path it
--- would normalize to.
---
--- @param text the path
--- @param kind 0 for the parent, 1 the file name, 2 the stem, 3 the extension
--- @param windows whether Windows rules apply
--- @return the piece, or nil where the path has none
function pathtext.part(text: string, kind: integer, windows: boolean): string?
    local start, length, componentKind, anchored = lastComponent(text, windows)
    if kind == 0 then
        -- A path that is only a root or a prefix has no parent: there is
        -- nowhere further up to go.
        if start == nil or componentKind == pathtext.ROOT or componentKind == pathtext.PREFIX then
            return nil
        end

        return pathtext.finish(text:sub(1, beforeLast(text, start as integer, anchored, windows)), windows)
    end
    if start == nil or componentKind ~= pathtext.NORMAL then
        return nil
    end
    local found = start as integer
    local stemLength, extensionAt, extensionLength = splitNameAt(text, found, length)
    if kind == 1 then
        return pathtext.finish(text:sub(found, found + length - 1), windows)
    elseif kind == 2 then
        return pathtext.finish(text:sub(found, found + stemLength - 1), windows)
    elseif extensionAt ~= nil then
        local at = extensionAt as integer

        return pathtext.finish(text:sub(at, at + extensionLength - 1), windows)
    end

    return nil
end

export = pathtext
